query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy is a solid refrigeration working medium that exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack. What single intervention could increase its integrity while preserving caloric performance in these operating regimes? State one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, predicted integrity and caloric outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, applicable field, pressure, temperature, and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a minor interstitial addition of 0.2 at.% boron (substituting for Si) into the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy will strengthen grain-boundary cohesion and refine the grain structure, thereby increasing fracture toughness and suppressing transformation-induced cracking while leaving the first-order magneto- and barocaloric responses essentially unchanged (ΔS and ΔT within ±5 %) under the usual magnetic-field (≤2 T) and hydrostatic-pressure (≤1 GPa) operating windows.
generation.material_initial_state: Arc-melted and annealed equiatomic high-entropy alloy (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38, polycrystalline, coarse grains, exhibiting a first-order magneto-structural transition near 300 K and a large ΔS but prone to intergranular cracking on cyclic magnetic or pressure loading.
generation.intervention: Add 0.2 at.% B (replacing an equal atomic fraction of Si) during melting, followed by identical homogenisation at 1273 K for 24 h and water quench.
generation.conditions: Magnetocaloric tests: 0–2 T applied field, 250–350 K.  Barocaloric tests: 0–1 GPa hydrostatic pressure, 250–350 K.  Mechanical integrity: room-temperature uniaxial compression up to 1 GPa, cycling 100 times.
generation.structural_mediator: Boron segregation to grain boundaries and possible formation of nm-scale Fe–B complexions increase boundary cohesive energy and slightly refine grains during solidification.
generation.mechanism: Stronger, more ductile grain boundaries retard the nucleation and propagation of transformation-induced intergranular cracks that originate from the 2–4 % volume change at the martensitic transition, while the very low B concentration does not significantly modify the parent and product crystal structures or the electronic density of states that controls ΔS and ΔT in magneto-/barocaloric cycles.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the baseline alloy: (1) Plane-strain fracture toughness (K_IC) rises by ≥50 %; compressive plastic strain to failure rises from <0.5 % to >1 %. (2) Peak isothermal magnetic entropy change (ΔS_M) at 2 T and ~300 K changes by <5 %. (3) Peak barocaloric entropy change (ΔS_p) at 1 GPa changes by <5 %. (4) After 100 magnetocaloric or barocaloric cycles, micro-crack density is reduced by ≥70 %.
generation.baseline: Unmodified (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy processed identically but without B; typical K_IC ≈ 8 MPa√m, plastic strain <0.5 %, peak ΔS_M ≈ 20 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 2 T, and severe intergranular cracking after ≤20 cycles.
generation.boundary: Valid for total B additions between 0.05 and 0.5 at.%, homogeneous solidification without coarse boride precipitation, and operating temperatures within ±50 K of the transition temperature (~300 K). Outside this range, excess borides or shifted transitions may degrade caloric output.
generation.uncertainty: If boron forms coarse Fe–B or Mn–B borides during solidification, magnetocaloric entropy change could drop more than anticipated; grain-boundary segregation levels and exact cohesive-energy gains are presently unverified.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two alloy buttons: (a) baseline composition, (b) +0.2 at.% B. Homogenise 24 h/1273 K, water-quench.  • Mechanical integrity: machine compact compression samples (Ø3 mm×4.5 mm), perform room-temperature cyclic compression to 1 GPa for 100 cycles, record plastic strain and crack density (SEM). Measure K_IC by chevron-notch bending.  • Caloric performance: measure M(H) isotherms (0–2 T) and V(P) isotherms (0–1 GPa) every 5 K from 250–350 K; compute ΔS_M and ΔS_p by Maxwell relations.
measurements: Peak ΔS_M (J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 2 T
Peak ΔS_p (J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 1 GPa
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if either: (i) K_IC of B-doped alloy is <1.2× that of baseline OR plastic strain increase <0.2 %; OR (ii) Peak ΔS_M or ΔS_p of B-doped alloy differs from baseline by >10 % in magnitude or the transition temperature shifts by >10 K.
